tools.description: Which consumers have configured access to, and which have independently observed usage of, an API Operation, an application Service or a gateway Route, for one gateway instance, environment and measurement window. Configured access and usage are separate propositions; unresolved associations stay explicit; nothing is inferred from names, hosts or paths. A consumer is the APISIX username on that gateway instance (source-qualified), not an application or person. With request.mode "evidence", the same tool resolves exact evidence refs from such an answer at the supplied snapshot.

ApiConsumerUsageEvidenceRequest.description:
`mode: "evidence"` (D3, D9): the query context is resubmitted so the service can rebuild the
ref map at the exact snapshot.
ApiConsumerUsageEvidenceRequest.title: ApiConsumerUsageEvidenceRequest

ApiConsumerUsageQueryRequest.description:
`mode: "query"` (D3). A reversed window is accepted: an I2 window with `window_start >=
window_end` is accepted-but-invalid and must stay addressable.
ApiConsumerUsageQueryRequest.title: ApiConsumerUsageQueryRequest

ApiConsumerUsageRequest.description: The single MCP `request` argument (D1): one of the two modes, discriminated on `mode`.
ApiConsumerUsageRequest.title: ApiConsumerUsageRequest

ApiUsageTarget.description:
D3: exactly one exact target. The id pattern depends on the kind; never a display name, path
or host.
ApiUsageTarget.title: ApiUsageTarget

ApiConsumerUsageEvidenceData.description: D9: the `mode: "evidence"` payload, one entry per requested ref, sorted by ref.
ApiConsumerUsageEvidenceData.title: ApiConsumerUsageEvidenceData

ApiUsageLimitationCode.description:

locality enum. The first five are refusal codes.
ApiUsageLimitationCode.title: ApiUsageLimitationCode

ApiUsageRequestContext.description: D4: the normalized query context (without `limit`, `cursor` and `snapshot_id`).
ApiUsageRequestContext.title: ApiUsageRequestContext

ApiUsageRow.description: D4: one I2 `qualification_rows` entry, enriched only with same-snapshot reconciliation.
ApiUsageRow.title: ApiUsageRow

ApiUsageTarget.description:
D3: exactly one exact target. The id pattern depends on the kind; never a display name, path
or host.
ApiUsageTarget.title: ApiUsageTarget

ApiUsageWindow.description: D4: the I2 window the answer is about. `valid` is true iff there are no reasons.
ApiUsageWindow.title: ApiUsageWindow

AssociationCounts.title: AssociationCounts

AssociationSummary.description:
Exactly one chain: `route_operation` for an `API_OPERATION` target, `target_service` for an

AssociationSummary.title: AssociationSummary

EvidenceEntry.description:
D9: one requested ref. A forged, cross-snapshot and cross-context ref are all simply
`NOT_RESOLVED` and indistinguishable (no ref history is kept).
EvidenceEntry.title: EvidenceEntry

MeasurementCode.description:
Every I2 limitation code a Route or row can carry: the window reasons and the route-level
coverage codes (contract §7).
MeasurementCode.title: MeasurementCode

RouteOperationReconciliationEvidence.description:
Only what the frozen I2 snapshot carries (D9 provenance boundary): the outcome, the raw

RouteOperationReconciliationEvidence.title: RouteOperationReconciliationEvidence

RowApi.description: The Route -> Operation -> contract-version chain, with the I2 outcomes unrenamed.
RowApi.title: RowApi

RowConsumer.description: D7: `source_name` is the APISIX Consumer username, a source-qualified identity.
RowConsumer.title: RowConsumer

RowUsage.description:
The usage proposition. The counts are omitted, never zero, when I2 could not establish them
(an invalid window); the interaction id is an opaque row-local value (D4).
RowUsage.title: RowUsage

SelectedRoute.description: D4: a Route selected by the target, emitted independently of `rows`.
SelectedRoute.title: SelectedRoute

outputSchema.description:
The 0.7 envelope (D2, D6). `data` is null if and only if the answer is a refusal (a
pre-evaluation failure); an evaluated `NOT_ANSWERED` still carries its payload.

tools.description: Direct service dependencies whose current evidence qualification shows a declared-versus-observed discrepancy, bound to the same stable snapshot.

ArchitectureDriftRequest.description:
v0.4.0 I3.1 - the `get_architecture_drift` request shape (I3 spec §9). Its field validation is
equivalent to `ServiceDependenciesRequest`'s (§9), but it is a separate public contract type
(§9.1): request-shape equality today is not permanent semantic identity, and the third tool needs
its own executable contract. The three field declarations are therefore deliberately restated
from the same private constants rather than inherited - `ServiceDependenciesRequest` is an
already-qualified I1 contract whose advertised MCP `inputSchema` is derived from it, and it stays
untouched. `tests/unit/test_architecture_intelligence_contracts.py` pins the equivalence so the
restatement cannot silently drift. Observation-context *normalization* is not duplicated (§9.1):
both types carry the same `ObservationContextInput`, and both are normalized by the single
`app.architecture_intelligence.observation_context.build_observation_context_ref`.
ArchitectureDriftRequest.title: ArchitectureDriftRequest

tools.name: get_architecture_drift

ArchitectureDriftData.description:
v0.4.0 I3.1 - spec §10. Deliberately only the service and the drift claim ids: no
`observed_only[]`/`not_observed[]` buckets, no `severity`/`score`/`summary_text` (spec §10 names
each of those as prohibited), because every returned `DependencyClaim` already carries the
authoritative `qualification` that made it drift. The claims themselves stay on the enclosing
`ArchitectureAnswer.claims` - this data payload only names them, in the same order.
ArchitectureDriftData.title: ArchitectureDriftData

DeploymentClaim.description:
I3 spec §12: the public `Service -[DEPLOYED_AS]-> Workload` claim. Deliberately has no
`delivery`/`qualification`/`coverage`/`destination_resolution` fields - those are
`DependencyClaim`-only concepts describing a CALLS/SENDS interaction, and `DEPLOYED_AS` is never
an interaction (spec §1: "DEPLOYED_AS != CALLS != SENDS != RECEIVES_FROM").
DeploymentClaim.title: DeploymentClaim

DeploymentResolutionMethod.description:
I3 spec §10.1: only the three *successful* identity-path outcomes - never CONFLICT/
AMBIGUOUS/UNRESOLVED, which are never a "method" a claim can be supported by. Compare
`DeploymentResolutionStatus` below, which is the wider 6-value outcome set a
`DeploymentResolution` (as opposed to an actual `DeploymentClaim`) may carry.
DeploymentResolutionMethod.title: DeploymentResolutionMethod

WorkloadKind.description:
I3 spec §8.1: the exact supported Kubernetes controller kinds a deployment identity path may
resolve to - the same closed set I2's own owner-chain resolution already admits.
WorkloadKind.title: WorkloadKind

WorkloadRef.description:
I3 spec §11: a bounded public Workload reference, deliberately its own model rather than an
`EntityRef` extension. `EntityRef` is reused by `DependencyClaim.subject`/`.object` and
`DeliveryRef.via` - widening its type-specific-field validator with a WORKLOAD branch would make
a Workload-shaped `EntityRef` constructible inside a dependency claim, exactly the governing
"DEPLOYED_AS != CALLS" / entity-equivalence boundary spec §1 forbids. `DeploymentClaim.object` is
typed `WorkloadRef`, never `EntityRef`, for the same reason.

tools.description: Which Services AIP can evidence-qualify as consumers of one Kafka Topic, for one broker and environment: each Kafka consumer group attached to the Topic at capture time T, with its Service attribution (RESOLVED, UNRESOLVED, AMBIGUOUS or CONFLICT) from explicit mapping evidence. Attachment is not message processing and the list is never complete: each capture covers only its configured groups. With request.mode "evidence", the same tool resolves exact evidence refs from such an answer at the supplied snapshot; evidence_refs must be duplicate-free and sorted in ascending order as plain strings. In query mode, destination_id is the canonical Topic id (topic:owned:..., as returned in get_service_dependencies), never a topic name; broker_id is the stable broker id (the name of the BrokerRef, such as kafka:...), not the canonical Broker id broker:owned:...

`mode: "evidence"` (spec §4): the exact snapshot, the same query context and 1-20 refs. The
service rebuilds the ref map of that context at that snapshot; there is no ref history.

destination_id.description: Exact canonical Kafka Topic id (`topic:owned:…`), not a topic name.
destination_id.title: Destination Id

topic_id.title: Topic Id

One accepted I1 capture of the requested broker and environment, with its own T (spec §3:

CaptureSource.title: CaptureSource

DestinationConsumersEvidenceData.title: DestinationConsumersEvidenceData

LimitationCode.title: LimitationCode

The mapping path: one accepted mapping entry for group G, as written by the operator, and the

RequestContext.description:
Spec §2: the exact query context. Page position, `limit` and `snapshot_id` are not part of

broker_id.description: Declared broker id (`x-aip-broker-id`, e.g. `kafka:cluster-a`), not a bootstrap address.
broker_id.title: Broker Id

destination_id.description: Exact canonical Kafka Topic id (`topic:owned:…`), not a topic name.
destination_id.title: Destination Id

RequestContext.title: RequestContext

RowLimitation.description: A non-resolving mapping entry of a RESOLVED group, with the ref of its mapping evidence.
RowLimitation.title: RowLimitation

outputSchema.description:
The 0.7.1 envelope. `data` is null if and only if the answer is a refusal. An evaluated
query is always `PARTIAL`: an accepted capture covers only its configured group allow-list at
its own T, so `CAPTURE_SCOPE_LIMITED` is always present and no answer claims completeness. An
evaluated evidence answer is `ANSWERED` when every ref resolved, `PARTIAL` when some did and
`NOT_ANSWERED` when none did.
outputSchema.title: DestinationConsumersAnswer
